description: Which public wallet lists and exchanges already carry a Robinhood Chain token, and what Robinhood's own public pages show for its symbol, read from each source without a key. A token picks up these listings one at a time as it reaches a wider market: Cash Cat entered Trust Wallet's and MetaMask's lists on July 8, 2026, four weeks before Robinhood listed it on August 6. On its own a sighting says little: most tokens on these lists are never listed by Robinhood. Pass the token's contract address as `token`; the `contract` of an entry from brainchain_custody_additions works. `token` can also be a symbol or name, such as RLUSD or Ripple USD, looked up on BitGo's lists for Robinhood Chain; when none there goes by it, on the lists the BrainChain MCP dataset records (Trust Wallet, MetaMask, LI.FI, CoinGecko, KuCoin and Gate); and when none there does either, among every token with a Uniswap pool by the symbol its contract gives itself (`pool index`). When exactly one token goes by it, `lookup` in the answer names the `contract` it stands for and its `source`, and for one found in the dataset the `dataset` day, block and manifest read; when several do, the answer lists them as `candidates`, each with its `source`, and reads nothing more. A symbol is whatever the token's deployer chose, so check the contract before relying on one found in the pool index. `lists` has an entry for Trust Wallet, MetaMask, LI.FI and CoinGecko, each with its `source` and `listed`. Trust Wallet and MetaMask keep one file for each token in their public code. When the token is listed, their entries add `link`, a link to that file, and `since`, when the list's master branch took the file: the time the pull request that added it was merged, which can be days after its commit was made. `since` is left out when that time cannot be shown: the file reached master without a pull request, it has more commits than GitHub's feed of them shows, or GitHub could not be read just now. Each `since` takes one of the 60 requests an hour GitHub allows one IP address without a key, or of the allowance of the GITHUB_TOKEN the operator set, and is kept while the server runs. Trust Wallet also keeps a file for a token it warns about or has dropped: its entry then has `listed` false and a `status` of `spam` or `abandoned`. `exchanges` has an entry for KuCoin and Gate, each with its `source`, `listed` and, when listed, whether `deposits` and `withdrawals` are open. All six are matched by the token's contract address. The tool reads the chain only for the time of `atBlock`, so an address that is not a token is listed nowhere. Robinhood and Bitstamp, which Robinhood owns, publish no contract addresses, so they are matched by symbol: `robinhood` has an entry for each `symbol` of letters and digits that the six sources give the token. `page` says whether Robinhood's crypto sitemap has a page for that symbol, `pair` whether the pair list Robinhood serves to API clients has it, with `pairsRead`, the number of pairs in that list when it was read, and `bitstamp` whether Bitstamp lists it on Robinhood Chain. That list leaves out most of the pairs Robinhood shows with a price only: on November 20, 2026 it held 140 pairs, while the sitemap had a page for each of the 353 pairs Robinhood's site shows. So `pair` false says only that this list does not have the symbol, and `page` is the field that covers price-only pairs. For a symbol in the list, `name` is Robinhood's own name for the asset and `tradable` says whether customers can trade it or only see its price. Two tokens can share a symbol, so compare that `name` with the token's own before reading an entry as this token: a token on Robinhood Chain that calls itself DOGE is not Dogecoin. An entry with a `page` and `pair` false has no name to compare, so it says only that Robinhood has a page under that symbol. `unread` names any source that could not be read just now: Trust Wallet, MetaMask, LI.FI, CoinGecko, KuCoin, Gate, Robinhood's site, Robinhood's pairs or Bitstamp. A list or exchange that could not be read has no entry, and a `robinhood` entry leaves out `page`, `pair` or `bitstamp` when its source could not be read. Neither is reported as unlisted. `token` holds the `contract` and the `symbol` and `name` the six sources give the token. `readAt` is when the answer was made. A list that was read is kept for ten minutes while the server runs, so what an entry says can be that old. To see only what was public at a point in the past, pass `atBlock`, a block number, or `at`, a time in ISO 8601 such as 2026-08-06T00:00:00Z; `until` then gives the time used (`at`), and the `block` for `atBlock`. A Trust Wallet or MetaMask entry stays when its `since` is at or before that time. The other sources publish no date for a listing, and a list's file can lack one, so a token listed there now may or may not have been listed then: `withheld` names each such source, with the `symbol` for Robinhood's site, Robinhood's pairs and Bitstamp, and the `link` or `status` of a list's file, and `lists`, `exchanges` and `robinhood` leave them out. A source that does not list the token now says nothing about then, so it has no entry. The first answer takes a few seconds, and later ones within those ten minutes come at once. Free, no key and no payment. Not advice.

at.description: Optional, in place of atBlock: a time in ISO 8601, such as 2026-08-06T00:00:00Z. Only the sightings public by then are listed.

atBlock.description: Optional: a block number. Only the sightings public by the end of that block are listed.

token.description: The token's contract address on Robinhood Chain, 0x followed by 40 hex characters, or its symbol or name, such as RLUSD.

name: brainchain_token_sightings
title: Where a Robinhood Chain token is already listed
